name: DFRobot 1.47" 172x320 IPS LCD Display Module (ST7789V3), 8-pin header and 18-pin GDI FPC
//: True of SKU DFR0995, board silkscreen 'V1.0', schematic V1.0 (2022/6/20). The pad list is the 8-pad header J1; the 18-pin GDI FPC (P1) carries the same signals and is not a pad list here. Header pitch is not published: pinrow8 assumes 2.54 mm. Only one side of the board was seen (DFRobot's back render and a front photo), never the part in hand.

needs.note: the backlight is on with BLK open (R1 10k to VCC on the transistor's base); drive it to dim or switch off

power.note: an on-board regulator U1 makes the 3 V the panel, buffer and backlight run at

body_mm.source: https://wiki.dfrobot.com/dfr0995/ specification table: Module Dimension 19.5mm x 44.5mm; the dimension drawing gives 44.5 x 19.5, PCB 1.6, 4.7 overall

supply_range_v.source: https://wiki.dfrobot.com/dfr0995/ pinout table: VCC 'DC3.3V-5V'; the same page's specification table says 'Operating Voltage 3.3V'
supply_range_v.why_it_matters: DFRobot's two texts disagree; 3.3 V is the only supply both name. The schematic's regulator U1 (part not named) suggests 5 V in is meant, but its limit is not published

full_screen_current_ma.source: not published on https://wiki.dfrobot.com/dfr0995/ or the schematic
full_screen_current_ma.why_it_matters: the rail sum cannot count the display; measure with the backlight on

peak_current_ma.source: not published: no figure for the backlight (3 white LEDs in parallel) at full brightness
peak_current_ma.why_it_matters: the rail sum names this part instead of summing it; measure on the bench with BLK open and a full white screen

input_high_v.source: not published: the inputs go through a 6-channel buffer U3 (part not named) powered from the 3 V regulator output
input_high_v.why_it_matters: that a 3.3 V host drives a safe high is assumed from the buffer's 3 V supply

input_low_v.why_it_matters: the low threshold is unknown; an ESP32 drives 0 V, which a 3 V buffer reads low

bus.source: https://wiki.dfrobot.com/dfr0995/ specification table: Interface SPI; write-only, no MISO on the header

driver_chip.source: https://wiki.dfrobot.com/dfr0995/ description: 'The ST7789V3 1.47 inch IPS Color Display Module'

value.BLK: 10k to VCC (R1) through 1k (R3): backlight on when BLK is open

on_board_pulls.source: module schematic R5, R10, R1 and R3, read from the drawing image
on_board_pulls.why_it_matters: RES and CS idle high without the host; with VCC at 5 V these pull the host's 3.3 V pins towards 5 V

series_resistors_ohm.source: module schematic R4, R6-R9 390R between the buffer U3 and the panel, read from the drawing image
series_resistors_ohm.why_it_matters: slows the edges; a high SPI clock may need testing

host_requirements: Power it from the host's 3V3: DFRobot's wiki says 'Operating Voltage 3.3V' in one table and 'DC3.3V-5V' in the other, and the schematic pulls RES, CS and BLK up to VCC, so at 5 V those pulls push a 3.3 V ESP32's pins above its supply.
The header's pad 1 end is read from the schematic image (J1: 1 BLK ... 8 VCC); match the silkscreen names on the board in hand before wiring, as a reversed row puts VCC on BLK.
The header pitch is not published; the record assumes 2.54 mm (pinrow8). Measure the board before a PCB is made.
The 18-pin GDI FPC (0.5 mm, reverse cable) carries the same signals: on a host's GDI socket the display takes that socket's SCLK, MOSI, DC, RES, CS and BLK pins; do not give them to another part.
Peak current (backlight at full) is not published; do not run it from a rail with no margin.

pin_order_proof.source: schematic J1 (CON8) numbers 1 BLK, 2 DC, 3 RES, 4 CS, 5 MOSI, 6 SCLK, 7 GND, 8 VCC, read from the drawing image; DFRobot's pinout render shows the silkscreen BLK DC RES CS MOSI SCLK GND VCC left to right, the same line. The wiki's text table lists the names VCC..BLK with no numbers.
pin_order_proof.why_it_matters: a row numbered from the wrong end puts VCC on BLK and GND on DC; read the silkscreen on the board in hand before wiring

legs.VCC: the pad at the end of the row nearest the GND pad, silkscreen VCC
legs.BLK: the pad at the other end, nearest the DFRobot logo, silkscreen BLK
